questions.question: The neighbour breathing factory smoke she was never paid for is bearing:
options: A negative externality — a cost outside the transaction
An opportunity cost of her own choices

questions.question: Because polluters do not pay the full cost of production, polluting products are:
The tragedy of the commons happens because each user:
options: Gains the full benefit of extra use while the cost of depletion is shared by all

questions.question: Which South African case matches the commons failure most directly?

subtopics.title: Protecting the Environment — the Policy Toolbox

questions.question: Emission standards, fishing quotas and environmental impact assessments belong to which tool family?
The carbon tax fixes the externality by:
options: Attaching the missing price to each ton of greenhouse gas, so the polluter faces the true cost

questions.question: Under tradable permits, total pollution is capped and:
options: Firms that cut cheaply sell permits to those that cannot, meeting the cap at lowest cost
Every firm must cut by an identical amount

questions.question: Community conservancies protect wildlife because:
options: Villages are forbidden from the land
Owners harvest sustainably when the future value belongs to them

subtopics.title: Sustainability — Living Off the Interest, Not the Capital

questions.question: The Brundtland definition says sustainable development meets present needs:
options: Without compromising future generations' ability to meet their own

questions.question: 'Living off the interest' means:
options: Investing in banks rather than nature
Harvesting no faster than natural stocks regenerate

questions.question: A renewable resource becomes non-renewable in practice when:
options: Use exceeds the threshold regeneration rate and the stock collapses

questions.question: For non-renewables like coal and platinum, sustainability means:
options: Converting the once-off proceeds into lasting assets like skills and infrastructure

subtopics.title: The Global and Local Impact on South Africa

questions.question: The injustice at the heart of climate negotiations is that:
options: The North built its wealth on two centuries of emissions while the South takes the earliest, hardest hits
The South emits most greenhouse gases
Emissions affect only the emitting country

questions.question: The 2022 Durban floods are cited as evidence of:
options: The heavier-rain end of climate change's loaded dice — over 400 deaths and billions in damage
A purely random event with no climate link

questions.question: Carbon border taxes threaten South African exports because:
options: Goods made with coal-fired electricity will pay penalties entering Northern markets

questions.question: South Africa's 'triple exposure' is as:
In the brick factory story, the 'invisible bill' is paid by:
options: The village downwind and downstream, who were never part of the deal

questions.question: Because the smoke's cost reaches no invoice, the market:
options: Orders more bricks — and more smoke — than the full cost would justify

questions.question: Each fisherman taking 'one more fish' empties the river because each is:
options: Individually sensible — full benefit to himself, shared cost to everyone

questions.question: Who is missing from the market's calculations in both stories?
options: Future generations, who place no orders today

subtopics.title: Putting a Price on the Smoke

questions.question: The plastic bag levy works by:
options: Making the bag cost something, so it stops being free and becomes a choice

questions.question: 'The market's own greed is harnessed' means that once smoke has a price:
options: Cutting pollution becomes profitable saving rather than charity

questions.question: Giving a village a permanent fishing quota flips behaviour because:
options: Next year's fish already belong to the owners, so gentle harvesting pays them
Quotas increase the fish population directly

questions.question: Countries sign climate agreements together mainly to:
options: Stop free-riding — one country cutting alone helps little and costs much

questions.question: 'Eat the harvest, never the seed' translates into economics as:
options: Use natural stocks slower than they renew

questions.question: 'Digging up the family gold to buy groceries' warns that non-renewable wealth should be:
options: Turned into lasting assets — skills, infrastructure, working towns
Divided equally among citizens in cash

questions.question: 'Save the park but starve the village beside it, and the village will not save the park' tests which leg of sustainability?
options: Social — costs and benefits must be shared fairly

questions.question: South Africa's just transition attempts to:
options: Close coal towns immediately with no support
Build clean energy fast while retraining workers and rebuilding coal regions, with wealthy nations helping to pay
